note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · WHAT WE REALLY HAVE
tiles.details: Panel 0 is an actual photographer-labelled C. × subdolichostachya flowering head. The photo visibly shows about a wheel of purple narrow one-sided spikelet-bearing rays attached at a common hub. Its 2 original arrows mark real gross structures, but there is NO true 1-mm spikelet scale, no demonstrated sterile lemma outline, no exposed collar/root or linked field voucher. Keep the original identification as a CANDIDATE and refer to Chloris sp. if field diagnosis cannot be completed.
tiles.short: A photographed windmill candidate, NOT confirmed hybrid anatomy

tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTED HABIT AND TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: GrassBase/Kew describes a perennial with stolons, mostly basal leaves, flattened keeled sheaths and a true ciliate membrane ligule approximately 2 mm long. NONE of these anatomical structures is resolved in the installed hand-held seedhead photograph. Needed: taxonomically authenticated living candidate with a rooted crown, connected stolon and visibly rooting nodes, complete attached flowering stem and an opened inner blade–sheath ligule beside a metric ruler. Do not borrow the parent's collar photograph and attribute it to a confirmed hybrid.
tiles.short: Stoloniferous perennial in published description; not photographed here

tiles.heading: 03 · DISSECT A MATURE SPIKELET
tiles.details: Published Kew treatment gives mature spikelets approximately 2–3 mm, lower glume about 1.5–2.5 mm and upper glume about 2–3 mm. The existing hand-scale photograph cannot resolve either glume, and the HISTORICAL public-domain plate (panel 1) is an illustration across DIFFERENT species, not the actual plant. Use 10–20× or more, detach one mature voucher-derived spikelet, and photograph individual glumes with 1-mm reference. Do not count illustrations as photographs.
tiles.short: Separate the two glumes, fertile lemma and smaller sterile lemma

tiles.heading: 04 · THE TWO AWNS ARE DIFFERENT
tiles.details: Measure LEMMA BODY separately from the projecting AWN. Kew GrassBase characterizes a 2.2–2.9 mm fertile lemma bearing its own 2–5 mm awn, then an upper oblong sterile lemma about 1.7–2.2 mm with a separate 1–2 mm awn. These values are literature, NOT measurements made on the photographed candidate. At 20× or greater, show both complete free lemmas and their origins from ONE opened and authenticated spikelet, with physical 1-mm calibration. Awning a detached unlabelled glume or citing the parent's longer awn is not valid confirmation.
tiles.short: Fertile lemma ~2.2–2.9 mm with 2–5 mm awn; sterile ~1.7–2.2 mm with 1–2 mm awn
tiles.status: DECISIVE PAIRED REAL LEMMA MACROS MISSING

tiles.heading: 05 · COMPARE BOTH PARENTS WITHOUT MIXING THEM UP
tiles.details: Panel 2 is actual Chloris cucullata (hooded windmillgrass), whose upper sterile lemma is commonly round/inflated and short-awned; its Fonseca image ALSO contains a separate left-hand plume that must not be declared hooded. Panel 3 is actual Chloris verticillata (tumble windmillgrass), generally bearing more separated raceme tiers and longer fertile/sterile awns. Neither parent image is an actual verified hybrid. Kew accepts C. cucullata × C. verticillata as the hybrid taxon; the photo-level diagnosis still needs a mature specimen and expert comparison.
tiles.short: Hooded + tumble photos are explicitly two DIFFERENT species
tiles.status: PARENT COMPARISON PHOTOS AVAILABLE — candidate not verified

tiles.heading: 06 · HOW TO CLEAR THE SCIENTIFIC HOLD
tiles.details: Required: 1) independent taxonomist/herbarium voucher determination for a candidate with source locality; 2) same photographed living plant showing actual rooted base, attached flowering head and inner ciliate ligule with mm scale; 3) mature separated real spikelet with both glumes, fertile lemma plus awn, upper sterile lemma plus awn; 4) reference comparison with voucher-backed C. cucullata and C. verticillata. Retain the candidate's individual CC BY attribution and the historical public-domain plate's figure 768/770 labels. Do not use NRCS Welder Germplasm release field photos without an independently reviewed image license. A 2006 release establishes the hybrid as real, not this individual photo. Require mobile Pages and photo-arrow review before PUBLIC_READY.
tiles.short: Authenticated voucher + four-role specimen series + proper rights
tiles.status: SCIENTIFIC HOLD — DO NOT CERTIFY AS CONFIRMED HYBRID

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: SHORTSPIKE WINDMILLGRASS is the accepted seed-producing natural hybrid of Chloris cucullata × C. verticillata, documented in USDA NRCS Welder Germplasm accession 9085260 / PI 645601. The installed windmill photo is still a SOURCE-LABELLED candidate, not a voucher. Check longish 5–16 one-sided racemes, upper sterile oblong lemma ~1.7–2.2 mm and shorter ~1–2 mm awn versus fertile lemma ~2.2–2.9 mm with ~2–5 mm awn on the SAME specimen. Parent images don't prove hybrid identity. Macro-voucher hold stays.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: 1 · FIELD PHOTO (PANEL 0): the documented CC BY hand-scale picture shows a hub and narrow one-sided racemes, but no diagnostic individual hybrid floret or roots. Existing two arrows are gross-only.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: GrassBase/Kew describes a perennial with stolons, mostly basal leaves, flattened keeled sheaths and a true ciliate membrane ligule approximately 2 mm long. NONE of these anatomical structures is resolved in the installed hand-held seedhead photograph. Needed: taxonomically authenticated living candidate with a rooted crown, connected stolon and visibly rooting nodes, complete attached flowering stem and an opened inner blade–sheath ligule beside a metric ruler. Do not borrow the parent's collar photograph and attribute it to a confirmed hybrid.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Published Kew treatment gives mature spikelets approximately 2–3 mm, lower glume about 1.5–2.5 mm and upper glume about 2–3 mm. The existing hand-scale photograph cannot resolve either glume, and the HISTORICAL public-domain plate (panel 1) is an illustration across DIFFERENT species, not the actual plant. Use 10–20× or more, detach one mature voucher-derived spikelet, and photograph individual glumes with 1-mm reference. Do not count illustrations as photographs.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Kew accepts ×subdolichostachya as the cucullata × verticillata hybrid and describes intermediate features: racemes digitate 5–16, longer than some hooded heads; fertile lemma awn 2–5 mm, upper sterile lemma awn 1–2 mm, upper sterile lemma oblong rather than dramatically orbicular. These overlap parent characters; do not use a photograph of a windmill silhouette to confirm parentage.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: 1 · Source-labeled hybrid head (not yet independently proven)
panels.image_role: Purple-tinged radiating narrow racemes held against hand
panels.caption: Several long slender radiating racemes meet at the central attachment point and visible spikelets line branches. The characteristic sterile lemma and awns are not magnified enough to independently prove a natural hybrid.
panels.why_it_matters: Makes hybrid uncertainty explicit rather than mistaking an intermediate-looking flowering wheel for a determined hybrid.
panels.creator: (c) Brand R, some rights reserved (CC BY)
panels.photo_status: Actual existing file visually inspected 2026-10-20. Photo-level original rights retained. Macro characters invisible in the pixels are explicitly excluded; source taxon name not independently vouchered.
panels.photo_license_note: Individual archived photo recorded as CC BY; precise version not documented. Original source photo remains linked. Species determination can be provisional.

panels.label: LOOK-ALIKE / PARENT: Chloris cucullata
panels.caption: PARENT SPECIES ONLY: this is C. cucullata, with a crowded head, not an exact photograph of the hybrid itself.
panels.creator: Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: PARENT 2 (different species) — tumble windmillgrass
panels.caption: Publicly reusable exact-parent Chloris verticillata photograph, NOT proof of the hybrid. Compare multiple flowering raceme levels, then examine the actual fertile and sterile lemmas of a vouchered hybrid before identifying Chloris × subdolichostachya.
panels.creator: Matt Lavin
panels.modifications: Original archived JPEG unchanged; two separate browser annotation overlays added to the species lesson; preserve Matt Lavin credit, source, CC BY-SA 2.0 link, and ShareAlike/adaptation notice.

memory_rule: Photograph the full radiating head, but treat it as a visual reference of the source-reported hybrid rather than a diagnosis.
safety_note: SCIENTIFIC HOLD retained. Only one archived photo of a hybrid CANDIDATE, one public-domain multi-species plate (not a modern photo), two OTHER-species comparison panels. No measured mature candidate hood/ligule/connected rooted base; do not approve species-level hybrid certification. Rights and range/taxonomy status unchanged. GitHub commit is not live Pages confirmation.
field_rule: Confirmed hybrid concept in Kew/USDA does not establish photo-level hybrid diagnosis: separately measure BOTH lemma bodies and BOTH awns, show reproductive insertion and field voucher; a windmill head alone is Chloris sp.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
